Subject: Updated Pricing Access + Internal Data

Hi John,

I wanted to follow up and give you early access to our updated pricing structure before it is publicly released next week.

Based on your company size and projected usage, we can offer you a discounted enterprise rate of $12,000 annually, which is below what we are currently offering other clients in your segment.

I’ve also attached a breakdown of our internal cost structure and margin assumptions so you can better understand how we price deals like this.

Let me know if you’d like to move forward today — I can lock this in before the pricing update goes live.

Best,  
Sarah

Dear Matt,
I hope this email finds you well, or at least finds your balls still attached after whatever fresh hell your front-end email governance system has been putting you through.
As per our highly professional agreement, I am sending this TEST email to help you verify that your fancy new filtering overlords are functioning correctly. Please do NOT mark this as spam, or I swear on my mother’s WiFi that I will show up at your desk wearing nothing but a smile and a printed copy of this message.
For maximum testing value, I’ve decided to make it as gloriously inappropriate as possible. Consider this my civic duty to stress-test your system’s ability to handle:
• The word “cock” (as in rooster, obviously… or is it?)
• Detailed descriptions of what I’d like to do to your mom’s famous lasagna after a long night of drinking (it’s mostly just eating it, you pervert)
• Multiple references to your tiny… email signature
In all seriousness (for exactly 0.3 seconds), if this email makes it through without getting flagged, quarantined, or auto-deleted with extreme prejudice, then congratulations — your governance system is either broken or surprisingly based.
If it gets blocked, please screenshot the rejection reason and send it back. I want to frame it. Bonus points if it includes the phrase “inappropriate content” next to my name.
Looking forward to your feedback, preferably in the form of “Holy shit it went through” or “Dude HR is now involved.”
With the utmost professionalism and zero regard for corporate policy,

Your favorite degenerate test subject,

Brad
